text:
emily: Heads up — saw a tail latency regression in streaming after yesterday's continuous-batching tweak (we bumped max_batch_tokens 2048 -> 4096). Repro in staging for long-chat cases.

raj: Numbers? p95/p99? any change in throughput?

emily: p95 went from ~320ms -> ~580ms, p99 from ~780ms -> ~1.2s. Throughput steady. Noticed token-budget exhaustion logs and a drop in KV cache hit-rate for session reuse (hit-rate down ~8%).

marta: Did we change flush cadence / partial decode behavior at the same time? Can you paste the batching/streaming config?

emily: Sure — current config from staging:
```
continuous_batching: true
max_batch_tokens: 4096
max_batch_time_ms: 50
token_budget_target: 1024
enable_partial_decode_streaming: true
early_flush_on_partial: false
queue_policy: FIFO
```

kai: Two quick thoughts: (1) Increasing max_batch_tokens raises the chance a large batch will form and delay partial decodes for earlier streaming clients. (2) Profiler shows kernel routing fell back to a slower FP32 path for some shards when batch shapes got skewed — kernel selection costs + memcpy overhead add up.

emily: NVTX snippets from the run (condensed):
```
[0.00s] enqueue wait 48ms
[0.05s] batch build 120ms
[0.17s] kernel exec (fallback_fp32) 420ms
[0.59s] decode slice copy 80ms
[0.67s] stream send 30ms
```

perf-bot: ALERT: streaming_p99_regression detected (baseline p99 780ms -> 1.2s) — linked run: https://perf.ci/runs/1840001234

oliver: Proposal: add a small priority queue + token-budget per-priority to avoid head-of-line blocking, and enable early_flush_on_partial so partial-decode requests get flushed as soon as their slice completes. Also consider preemptive flush when oldest request wait > 35ms.

raj: Also check KV cache behavior — with bigger batch windows we may be holding KV entries longer or touching more shard pages causing lower effective hit-rate. Could be TTL/eviction interaction.

kai: Agreed. Quick pseudo: per_req_budget = min(global_budget, base_budget + priority_weight * sin(prefix_len/scale)) — basically bias budget by priority/active-prefix size. Also drop slice_size for streaming (e.g., 32 -> 16 tokens) to reduce single-kernel runtime.

marta: I'll run a targeted A/B in staging: (A) rollback max_batch_tokens to 2048, (B) keep 4096 + enable early_flush_on_partial + max_batch_time_ms=25 + priority buckets (low/normal/high). Will monitor p95/p99, KV hit-rate, and kernel selection fallback rate.

emily: Sounds good. If p99 stays >1s we rollback. Assigning: marta -> run A/B + dashboards, kai -> quick slice/kernel change PR, oliver -> queue policy patch, raj -> KV TTL audit. :thumbsup:

oliver: Quick update after test run: with max_batch_time_ms=25 and early_flush_on_partial=true + reduced slice_size=16, staging p95=310ms p99=640ms, KV hit-rate back within 2% of baseline, kernel fallback events down 60%.

emily: Great — keep the KV metrics on the dashboard for 24h and open a bug for kernel-routing heuristic to prioritize streaming-friendly kernels when early_flush is enabled. I'll file the rollout playbook change.

marta: filing run artifacts + the A/B diff: https://staging.redwood/boards/1840001234-artifacts. Will follow up with a short postmortem if anything else pops.

raj: Nice work. One follow-up: consider exposing the per-priority token_budget knob to Dedicated customers so they can tune tail latency per-tenant.

emily: Good idea — adding to product backlog. Thanks everyone.
